plans.name: SI Joint Stability & Pelvic Rebalancing
plans.tags: si joint pelvis sacrum pelvic pain hip
plans.objective: 3-phase plan for SI joint alignment and pelvic stability

phases.name: Phase 1: Reset & Realign
phases.goal: Reduce inflammation, calm overactive muscles, unlock mobility
phases.focus: Decompression, Muscle Inhibition, Gentle Joint Mobilization

exercises.name: Supine 90-90 Decompression
exercises.description: Lie flat on your back with your lower legs supported on a chair or bench. Hips and knees at 90 degrees. Arms by your sides, palms up. Inhale through nose for 4 seconds, exhale through mouth for 6. Let your lower back melt into the floor. Reduces pressure on SI joints and promotes parasympathetic activation.

exercises.name: SI Joint Reset (Muscle Energy Technique)
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees bent. Cross right ankle over left knee. Place right hand on inside of right knee. Gently push knee outward while resisting with your leg. Hold 5 seconds, release. Repeat 5 times, switch sides. Rebalances tension between sacrum and ilium.

exercises.name: Figure 4 Rock
exercises.description: In the same position, gently rock your hips side to side about 1-2 inches each direction. You should feel gentle movement deep in the glute and SI joint region. Mobilizes the joint and reduces gluteal tension.

exercises.name: QL & Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: QL: Stand tall, reach right arm overhead, lean left. Feel stretch from ribs to hip. Hip Flexor: Kneel on right knee, left foot forward. Tuck pelvis, activate glutes, shift forward. Raise arms overhead to deepen.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.description: Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat. Slowly tilt pelvis so lower back flattens into floor. Hold 3 seconds, release. Use lower abdominals without squeezing glutes. Builds foundational core-pelvic connection.

phases.name: Phase 2: Stabilize & Activate
phases.goal: Strengthen stabilizing muscles of the pelvis and core
phases.focus: Glute Medius Activation, Core Bracing, Anti-Rotation Control

exercises.name: Glute Bridge Hold
exercises.description: Lie on back, feet flat, hip-width apart. Drive through heels, lift hips. Straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze glutes hard at top. Don't arch back — ribs down, core tight.

exercises.name: Clamshells
exercises.description: Lie on left side, knees bent, feet together. Stack hips. Lift top knee without rolling backward or separating feet. Lower slowly. Add resistance band above knees for extra challenge.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lie on back, arms up, knees bent 90 degrees. Brace core. Slowly extend right leg and left arm without letting back arch off floor. Return and switch. Improves deep abdominal control.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Hikes
exercises.description: Stand on a step with right foot. Left foot hangs freely. Let left hip drop slightly, then use right glute and side body to lift it back up. Control each rep. Switch sides.

exercises.name: Wall Posture Drill
exercises.description: Stand with heels, glutes, upper back, and head against wall. Slightly tuck pelvis, draw ribs down. Lightly brace core and breathe. Builds awareness of optimal posture.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.description: Band around thighs or above knees. Slight squat, knees aligned. Step sideways slowly, maintaining tension. Engage glutes each step. Both directions.

phases.name: Phase 3: Integrate & Maintain
phases.goal: Improve pelvic control under dynamic load for daily function
phases.focus: Functional Core Strength, Balance, Real-Life Movement Control

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lie on back, bend one knee, extend opposite leg. Drive through grounded heel to lift hips. Keep hips level. Challenges glute strength and single-leg stability.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Hands and knees. Extend right arm and left leg, keeping hips and shoulders level. Hold 5 seconds. Return slowly, switch. Slow, steady movement.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.description: Anchor resistance band at chest height. Stand perpendicular. Hold band at chest, press straight out. Resist rotation. Builds anti-rotation core control crucial for SI joint stability.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.description: Hold equal-weight dumbbells or kettlebells. Stand tall, brace core, walk slowly. Don't let shoulders dip or sway. Focus on posture, balance, spinal alignment.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance + Reach
exercises.description: Stand on one foot. Slowly reach opposite hand forward and slightly down as if touching the floor. Maintain balance and control. Strengthens glutes, challenges proprioception.

lifestyle: Avoid standing with weight shifted onto one hip
Don't cross the same leg while sitting — alternate sides
Sleep with a pillow between your knees for hip alignment
Switch shoulders or arms when carrying bags or children
Drink water consistently to keep joints and ligaments hydrated
If pain flares, return to Phase 1 and reduce intensity temporarily
plans.maintenance: 1x Reset Day (Phase 1) · 2x Stability Days (Phase 2) · 1x Integration Day (Phase 3) · Reassess every 6 weeks

plans.name: Anterior Pelvic Tilt Correction
plans.tags: anterior pelvic tilt APT hip flexor tight psoas lordosis swayback posture pelvis glutes core lower back
plans.objective: Correct excessive anterior pelvic tilt by releasing tight hip flexors, strengthening glutes and core, and retraining neutral pelvic alignment.

phases.name: Phase 1: Release & Reset
phases.goal: Reduce tightness in hip flexors, quads, and lumbar extensors that pull the pelvis forward
phases.focus: Hip Flexor Lengthening • Lumbar Decompression • Pelvic Awareness

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front of you (both knees at 90°). Tuck your tailbone under by squeezing your right glute. Gently shift your weight forward until you feel a deep stretch in the front of your right hip. Raise your right arm overhead and lean slightly to the left to deepen the stretch into the psoas and iliacus. Do not arch your lower back. The goal is to lengthen the muscles pulling your pelvis into tilt, not to push through pain.

exercises.name: Rectus Femoris Couch Stretch
exercises.description: Kneel with your back to a couch or wall. Place your right foot up on the couch behind you (top of foot flat against the cushion). Step your left foot forward into a lunge position. Keep your torso tall and tuck your pelvis under. You should feel an intense stretch down the front of your right thigh and hip. The rectus femoris crosses both the hip and knee joints and is one of the primary drivers of anterior pelvic tilt when shortened. If this is too intense, move your front foot further forward.

exercises.name: Supine Psoas Release (90-90 Position)
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your calves resting on a chair so that your hips and knees are both at 90°. Let your arms rest at your sides, palms up. Breathe slowly and deeply (inhale 4 seconds through nose, exhale 6-8 seconds through mouth). Allow your lower back to settle into the floor naturally. This position takes the psoas completely off tension and allows the lumbar spine to decompress. Your lower back should feel like it is melting into the ground.

exercises.name: Prone Quad/Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Lie face down. Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grab your ankle or foot. Gently pull your heel toward your glute while pressing your hip bone into the floor. Keep your core lightly braced so your lower back does not arch excessively. You should feel a stretch along the entire front of your thigh and into the hip. If you cannot reach your foot, loop a towel or band around your ankle.

exercises.name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt Practice (Wall)
exercises.description: Stand with your back against a wall, feet about 6 inches from the base. You will notice a gap between your lower back and the wall. Slowly tilt your pelvis backward (think about bringing your belt buckle up toward your ribs) so that your lower back flattens against the wall. Hold for 3 seconds, then release. This is the foundational movement that teaches your body what a neutral or slightly posterior pelvic position feels like. Master this before progressing.

exercises.name: Foam Roll Quads and Hip Flexors
exercises.description: Lie face down on a foam roller positioned under the front of one thigh. Roll slowly from just above the knee to the hip crease. When you find a tender spot, pause and hold for 10-15 seconds while breathing deeply. Then continue. Roll the inside of the thigh slightly to target the vastus medialis, and the outside slightly for the IT band/TFL junction. The TFL is a commonly overlooked contributor to anterior pelvic tilt.

phases.name: Phase 2: Activate & Strengthen
phases.goal: Strengthen the glutes, deep abdominals, and hamstrings that posteriorly tilt and stabilize the pelvis
phases.focus: Glute Activation • Deep Core Bracing • Hamstring Engagement • Anti-Extension Control

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with Posterior Tilt
exercises.rx: 3 sets of 12 reps, 3 sec hold at top
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart. Before lifting, tilt your pelvis posteriorly so your lower back is flat on the floor. Maintain that pelvic position as you drive through your heels and lift your hips. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for 3 seconds. Your ribs should stay down and your lower back should not arch. Slowly lower. This version specifically trains the glute-core connection needed to hold your pelvis in a corrected position.

exercises.name: Dead Bug (Anti-Extension Focus)
exercises.description: Lie on your back with arms extended toward the ceiling and knees bent at 90°. Press your lower back into the floor by engaging your deep abdominals. Slowly extend your right leg and left arm toward the floor without letting your lower back lift off the ground. If your back arches at all, you have gone too far. Return and switch sides. This trains the transverse abdominis and internal obliques, the muscles that resist the forward pull of anterior pelvic tilt.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank Bridge
exercises.description: Sit on the floor with legs extended and hands behind you, fingers pointing forward. Press through your hands and heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to ankles. Squeeze your glutes and push your hips toward the ceiling. Keep your chin slightly tucked. This simultaneously strengthens glutes, hamstrings, and posterior chain while stretching the hip flexors under load.

exercises.name: Standing Cable or Band Pull-Through
exercises.description: Anchor a resistance band low behind you. Straddle the band facing away from the anchor. Hinge at your hips (push them backward), keeping a slight bend in your knees and your back flat. Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes to return to standing. At the top, tuck your pelvis slightly and stand tall. This teaches your glutes to control the pelvis through a hip hinge pattern, one of the most functional movement corrections for anterior pelvic tilt.

exercises.name: Plank with Posterior Pelvic Tilt
exercises.description: Set up in a forearm plank. Instead of holding a flat back, deliberately tuck your tailbone under by squeezing your glutes and drawing your belt buckle toward your chin. You should feel your lower abs engage intensely. Your lower back should be slightly rounded, not arched. This corrective plank teaches you to maintain pelvic control under load and is far more effective than a standard plank for anterior pelvic tilt.

exercises.name: Hamstring Walkouts
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Lift your hips into a bridge and hold. From this position, slowly walk your feet out one step at a time until your legs are nearly straight, then walk them back in. Keep your hips elevated the entire time. This eccentrically loads the hamstrings in a lengthened position, building the posterior chain strength needed to counterbalance dominant hip flexors.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction (Glute Med)
exercises.description: Lie on your side with your body in a straight line. Keep your top leg straight and slightly behind your body (about 10° of hip extension). Lift the top leg toward the ceiling, leading with your heel, not your toes. Lower slowly. The slight extension bias ensures you target the posterior fibers of the glute medius, which help control lateral pelvic stability. If your hip flexors cramp, your leg is too far forward.

phases.name: Phase 3: Integrate & Retrain Posture
phases.goal: Build corrected pelvic alignment into standing, walking, and functional movement patterns
phases.focus: Functional Movement Patterns • Standing Posture Retraining • Dynamic Pelvic Control

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Light Load)
exercises.description: Hold light dumbbells or a kettlebell. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Hinge at your hips, pushing them straight back while keeping a flat back. Lower the weights along your shins until you feel a strong hamstring stretch. Drive back up by squeezing your glutes, finishing with a slight posterior tilt at the top. Do not hyperextend. This pattern teaches you to use your glutes and hamstrings as the primary hip extensors instead of relying on your lower back.

exercises.name: Step-Ups with Pelvic Control
exercises.description: Stand facing a box or step (12-18 inches). Place one foot fully on the step. Before stepping up, tuck your pelvis into a neutral or slightly posterior position. Drive through the heel of the top foot to stand up completely. Do not let your lower back arch or your hip drop on the standing side. Step down slowly. This integrates pelvic control into a real-world movement pattern like climbing stairs.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat with Pause
exercises.rx: 3 sets of 8 reps, 3 sec pause at bottom
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest. Squat down to parallel or just below. Pause for 3 seconds at the bottom and check your pelvic position: your tailbone should not tuck under excessively (butt wink) and your lower back should not arch. Stand by driving through your heels and squeezing your glutes at the top. The pause forces awareness and control.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lie on your back, bend one knee with foot flat, and extend the other leg straight. Posteriorly tilt your pelvis, then drive through the planted heel to lift your hips. Keep your hips level. Hold for 2 seconds at the top. This challenges single-leg glute strength and prevents your pelvis from rotating or tilting under asymmetric load.

exercises.name: Wall Posture Drill with Pelvic Correction
exercises.description: Stand with your heels, glutes, upper back, and head against a wall. You will likely notice a large gap between your lower back and the wall. Tuck your pelvis posteriorly to close that gap until you can just barely slide your hand between your back and the wall. Lightly brace your core, draw your ribs down, and breathe. This is your target standing posture. Practice transitioning from this wall position to standing freely, maintaining the same alignment.

exercises.name: Walking Posture Practice
exercises.description: During a portion of your daily walk, actively focus on pelvic position. Slightly tuck your pelvis, engage your lower abs gently, and lead with your glutes as you stride. Avoid leaning forward from your hips or arching your back. Think about your belt buckle pointing straight ahead, not tilted toward the floor. Over time, this corrected walking pattern will become automatic, but it takes deliberate practice for 4-6 weeks.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry with Posture Focus
exercises.description: Hold equal-weight dumbbells or kettlebells at your sides. Stand tall. Before you walk, set your pelvis into neutral by squeezing your glutes and lightly bracing your core. Walk slowly, keeping your shoulders level, spine tall, and pelvis stable. Do not allow your lower back to arch under the load. This reinforces postural alignment under functional load.

lifestyle: Avoid prolonged sitting in low, soft couches or chairs that encourage your pelvis to tilt forward. Use a firm surface and sit on your sit bones.
If you sit for work, set a timer every 30-45 minutes to stand, perform 5 posterior pelvic tilts, and do a 30-second hip flexor stretch per side.
Sleep on your back with a pillow under your knees to reduce hip flexor shortening overnight. If you sleep on your side, place a pillow between your knees and avoid pulling your knees up too high.

Stop stretching your hamstrings aggressively. In anterior pelvic tilt, hamstrings feel tight because they are being pulled long by the tilted pelvis, not because they are actually short. Stretching them more makes the problem worse.

Wear shoes with moderate heel drop (not high heels, not completely flat minimalist shoes) until your pelvic alignment improves. Elevated heels shift your center of gravity forward and worsen anterior tilt.
When standing for long periods, place one foot on a small step or ledge to reduce lumbar lordosis. Alternate feet every few minutes.
Strengthen before you stretch. The primary driver of correction is building glute and core strength, not just releasing tight muscles. If you only stretch and never strengthen, the tilt will return.
plans.maintenance: Daily: Hip flexor stretches (2-3 min per side) + posterior pelvic tilt practice (wall or supine). 3-4x/week: Full Phase 2 or Phase 3 workout. Weekly: 1x foam rolling session for quads, hip flexors, and TFL. Reassess your standing posture against a wall every 2 weeks to track progress. Expect noticeable improvement in 4-6 weeks with consistent effort.

plans.name: Weekend Joint Protection Plan
plans.tags: weekend joint protection knee hip SI arthritis errand recovery
plans.objective: Protect your knees, hips, and SI joints during active weekends so Monday doesn't hurt.

phases.name: Saturday Morning Prep
phases.goal: Warm up joints before activity
phases.focus: Joint mobilization • Glute activation • Light movement

exercises.name: Seated Knee Circles
exercises.description: Sit on a chair, gently lift one foot and rotate your lower leg in a circular motion. 10 circles clockwise, 10 counterclockwise per leg.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.description: Lay flat on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Flatten your lower back into the floor, then arch slightly. 10 slow reps.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
exercises.description: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips. Inhale—arch your back (cow), exhale—round your back (cat). 10 rounds, slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Glute Squeezes
exercises.description: Lie on your back or sit upright. Squeeze your glut muscles like you're trying to crack a walnut. 10 reps, hold each squeeze for 5 seconds.

exercises.name: Mini Squats to a Chair
exercises.description: Stand in front of a chair, lower slowly like you're about to sit—then stand back up. 5–8 reps. Use arms for support if needed.

phases.name: Evening Reset & Recover
phases.goal: Decompress and recover after a full day
phases.focus: Stretching • Glute strength • Breathing • Recovery

exercises.name: Wall Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: Lie on your back, one leg up against a wall, the other bent or flat on the floor. Hold 1 minute per leg.

exercises.name: Figure 4 Stretch
exercises.description: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Pull the uncrossed leg toward you gently. Hold 30 seconds per side.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.description: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Push through your heels and lift your hips. 10 reps, squeeze your glutes at the top.

exercises.name: 90/90 Breathing
exercises.description: Lie on your back, feet on a wall (knees/hips at 90°). One hand on chest, one on belly. 10 deep belly breaths. Relax your whole body.

exercises.name: Ice Therapy
exercises.description: Ice your knees or hip/SI joint for 10–15 minutes while relaxing—no direct contact with skin. Optional but powerful.

lifestyle: Turmeric + Ginger Capsules daily for anti-inflammatory support
Magnesium Glycinate (400mg at night) for muscle relaxation and sleep
Topical Arnica or Biofreeze for sore knees or hips before/after movement
Collagen Peptides daily to support joint tissues (add to coffee or smoothie)
Split errands into 2 smaller trips—don't do it all at once
Use a rolling cart or walker for longer walking distances
While standing in line, gently shift your weight side-to-side for SI joint relief
Take micro-breaks before pain starts—don't wait until it hurts to sit down
plans.maintenance: Repeat both routines every Saturday and Sunday. Do warm-up before activity, evening reset after. Come in Monday feeling more aligned, looser, and stronger.

plans.name: Low Back Relief Plan
plans.tags: low back pain L5 S1 standing core posture lumbar relief
plans.objective: Stabilize your spine, strengthen your core, and stand pain-free from L5–S1 discomfort.

phases.name: Daily Core Routine
phases.goal: Decompress the spine, activate deep core, relieve pressure from standing
phases.focus: Spinal decompression • Core activation • Posture rebuilding

exercises.name: Supine 90-90 Decompression
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your calves on a chair (hips & knees at 90°). Arms out, palms up. Breathe deeply: inhale 4 seconds, exhale 6 seconds. Relax and let your spine settle. If your back feels tight, place a towel under your hips.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.description: Stay on your back, knees bent. Gently flatten your low back into the floor. Rock your pelvis toward your nose, hold 3 sec, release. Don't use your glutes—let your lower abs do the work.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.description: Drive through heels and lift your hips. Squeeze glutes at the top for 5 sec. Slowly lower down. Keep your ribs tucked. Don't arch your back.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: On hands and knees. Extend right arm + left leg, hold 5 sec. Keep hips level—no wobbles. Switch sides. Balance a cup of water on your low back—don't spill it.

exercises.name: Wall Lean Posture Drill
exercises.description: Back flat against a wall (heels, glutes, shoulders, head all touching). Slightly tuck pelvis to bring low back toward the wall. Breathe and hold. Do it barefoot to boost foot-to-core connection.

phases.name: Mini Movement Breaks
phases.goal: Reset your spine and prevent pressure build-up
phases.frequency: Every 45-60 min of standing, take 2-3 min
phases.focus: Spinal reset • Active recovery • Movement variety

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squats
exercises.description: Perform 10 bodyweight squats to reset your spine during standing breaks.

exercises.name: Quick Bridges
exercises.description: Perform 5 bridges as a quick spinal reset during movement breaks.

exercises.name: Side-to-Side Stretching
exercises.description: Gentle side-to-side stretching and walking around your space to prevent pressure build-up.

phases.name: Foam Rolling
phases.goal: Release tight support muscles
phases.focus: Glutes • Quads • Hamstrings • IT Band/TFL

exercises.name: Foam Rolling Circuit
exercises.description: Roll glutes, quads, hamstrings, and IT Band/TFL. Move slow. Never roll directly over your spine.

lifestyle: Don't lock your knees when standing
Avoid leaning to one leg
Sleep with pillow between or under your knees
Wear proper shoes—no old or worn-out soles
Stay hydrated (your spinal discs are 80% water!)
Bring your shoes to Dr. Ray for a wear-pattern check
plans.maintenance: Daily core routine morning & evening (6x/week). Movement breaks every 45-60 min while standing. Foam rolling 2x/week. You'll feel better in days, move better in 1-2 weeks, stand longer pain-free in 3-4 weeks.

plans.name: Shoulder Pain Relief
plans.tags: shoulder pain AC joint scapular dysfunction hairdresser overhead repetitive
plans.objective: Decrease AC joint stress, stabilize scapular muscles, and improve shoulder posture.

phases.name: Acute Relief & Activation
phases.goal: Reduce inflammation, relieve acute discomfort, activate stabilizers
phases.focus: Inflammation control • Gentle mobilization • Postural reset

exercises.name: Ice Therapy
exercises.description: Apply ice over the AC joint using a gel pack or ice wrapped in a towel for 15 minutes, 2–3 times per day.

exercises.name: Pendulum Circles
exercises.description: Lean forward supporting body on a table with the opposite arm. Let painful arm dangle and gently circle it 10 times each direction.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions
exercises.description: Stand or sit with good posture. Squeeze shoulder blades together without shrugging shoulders. Hold 5 seconds, repeat 12–15 reps.

exercises.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
exercises.description: Place forearms on doorway, elbows at shoulder height. Step forward until stretch is felt in the chest. Hold 30 seconds.

exercises.name: Postural Reset Breaks
exercises.description: Set phone alarm every hour. 30 seconds: pull chin back, sit tall, squeeze shoulder blades.

phases.name: Rebuild & Stabilize
phases.goal: Build strength and control in postural and stabilizing muscles
phases.focus: Scapular strength • Rotator cuff stability • Thoracic mobility

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: Stand with back, arms, and hands against wall. Slide arms up and down like a snow angel without arching back.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-Ws
exercises.description: Lie face down. Y: Arms at 45°, thumbs up, lift 10 reps. T: Arms at 90°, palms down, lift 10 reps. W: Elbows bent, squeeze shoulder blades, 10 reps.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Rows
exercises.description: Anchor band at chest height. Pull elbows back, squeezing shoulder blades. 2–3 sets of 12 reps.

exercises.name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.description: Elbow at side, bent 90°. Press hand outward into wall without moving arm. Hold 10 seconds, 10 reps.

exercises.name: Thoracic Mobility Foam Rolling
exercises.description: Roll upper back gently for 2–3 minutes daily.

phases.name: Functional Reinforcement
phases.goal: Integrate posture, mobility, and control into real-world tasks
phases.focus: Dynamic stability • Functional strength • Work simulation

exercises.name: Wall Slides with Resistance Loop
exercises.description: Loop around wrists, slide arms up wall keeping tension. Focus on scapular upward rotation.

exercises.name: Standing Scaption with Light Dumbbells
exercises.description: Arms 30° from front, lift to shoulder height. 2–3 sets of 10 reps with 2–5 lb weights.

exercises.name: Serratus Wall Slide + Protraction
exercises.description: Slide arms up wall while pushing into it. At top, push hands slightly forward to activate serratus.

exercises.name: Banded Face Pulls
exercises.description: Pull resistance band toward face, elbows high, squeeze shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Functional Posture Practice
exercises.description: Mimic work positions with corrected posture. Practice shoulder blade control, neutral wrist, elbow alignment. Use a mirror or phone to observe posture for feedback.

lifestyle: Omega-3s (EPA/DHA), Turmeric + black pepper, and Magnesium glycinate for anti-inflammatory support
Avoid sleeping on painful shoulder; support arm with pillow if side sleeping
Diaphragmatic breathing 5 minutes daily to reduce tension and improve posture
plans.maintenance: If pain persists beyond 3 weeks or worsens, refer for imaging or further diagnostic evaluation. Ongoing maintenance and proper posture awareness are essential to prevent future flare-ups.

plans.name: Neck Pain & Cervico-Thoracic Support
plans.tags: neck pain cervical cervico-thoracic junction posture chin tuck mobility
plans.objective: Prevent recurrence of neck pain through spinal mobility, muscular balance, and posture correction.

phases.name: Daily Relief & Reset
phases.goal: Relieve acute neck pain and reset posture
phases.focus: Cervical decompression • Postural reset • Nervous system regulation

exercises.name: Cervical Retractions (Chin Tucks)
exercises.description: Sit or stand upright with good posture. Gently pull your chin straight back (not down) like you're making a double chin. Hold 5 seconds, repeat 10–15 times.

exercises.name: Suboccipital Release
exercises.description: Lie on the floor with a rolled towel or peanut ball under the base of the skull. Relax and breathe deeply for 2–3 minutes.

exercises.name: Wall Posture Reset
exercises.description: Stand against a wall: heels, glutes, upper back, and head all touching. Bring arms up so elbows are bent at 90 degrees like a goal post and press them against the wall. Hold 30 seconds.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.description: Lie on your back or sit in a chair with hands on your lower ribs. Inhale through your nose (expand ribs), exhale slowly through your mouth. 5 minutes to reduce neck tension and reset posture.

phases.name: Mobility + Stability
phases.goal: Build cervical mobility and mid-back stability
phases.focus: Cervical CARs • Thoracic activation • Isometric neck strength

exercises.name: Cat-Cow with Cervical Control
exercises.description: On hands and knees, slowly alternate between arching and rounding your spine. Add controlled head nods through the full range.

exercises.name: Cervical CARs
exercises.description: Sit or stand tall, slowly draw the biggest circle you can with your nose. Keep shoulders relaxed, avoid fast movements. Slow controlled circles help lubricate cervical joints and increase proprioception.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: With your back against the wall or floor, move your arms up and down while maintaining contact. Focus on mid-back activation and keeping your chin tucked.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Holds
exercises.description: Gently press your forehead into your hand (front), then the back of your head, then each side. Hold 5 seconds in each direction, repeat 2x through.

phases.name: Functional Reinforcement
phases.goal: Integrate postural strength into daily function
phases.focus: Scapular strengthening • Cervical-thoracic integration • Posture habits

exercises.name: Prone T/Y/W Activation
exercises.description: Lie face down, keeping neck neutral. T: arms out to the side. Y: arms at an angle overhead. W: elbows bent back. Lift arms slightly, hold for 3 seconds.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts or Rows
exercises.description: Using a resistance band, pull your hands apart at chest level or row backward. Focus on scapular movement, not shoulder shrugging.

exercises.name: Wall Lean Nod
exercises.description: Stand about 12 inches from a wall, lean back so your head and mid-back touch. Practice gentle chin tucks while engaging deep neck flexors and upper back.

exercises.name: Posture Break Protocol
exercises.description: Every hour, pause for 30 seconds: do a chin tuck, squeeze shoulder blades, take 3 deep breaths. Use alarms or sticky notes as reminders.

lifestyle: Cervical Orthotic Roll or Denneroll: 5-10 minutes daily for curve restoration (as advised by chiropractor)
Magnesium Glycinate (200-400mg) for muscle relaxation if tension is high
Blue Light Glasses to reduce forward head posture from screen use
Anti-inflammatory diet: minimize sugar and seed oils; increase hydration, omega-3s, and collagen-rich foods
Pair posture resets with daily habits (brushing teeth, waiting for coffee) to stay consistent
plans.maintenance: Choose 2-3 movements daily; vary based on how your neck feels. Respect pain—avoid pushing through sharp discomfort. Track flare-up patterns. Recheck progress with chiropractor every 4-6 weeks.

plans.name: Thoracic Mobility + Rib Cage Reset
plans.tags: thoracic mobility rib cage reset posture breathing upper back stiffness extension
plans.objective: Restore thoracic extension, improve rib cage mobility, and enhance breathing capacity.

phases.name: Mobilize & Breathe
phases.goal: Open restricted thoracic segments and unlock rib motion
phases.focus: Spinal Extension • Rib Mobility • Diaphragm Control

exercises.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extensions
exercises.description: Lie on a foam roller placed horizontally across your upper back (just below the shoulder blades). Support your head with your hands. Gently arch backward over the roller, extending through your upper spine. Avoid forcing the movement. Shift your body to roll up or down slightly between sets.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: Stand with your heels, glutes, upper back, and head against a wall. Raise your arms into a goalpost position. Slide your arms up and down slowly while maintaining wall contact. Do not let your shoulders shrug.

exercises.name: Seated Rib Cage Expansion Breathing
exercises.description: Sit upright with your hands placed on the sides of your rib cage. Inhale deeply through your nose, feeling your ribs expand outward and backward. Exhale slowly through your mouth. Focus on 360° rib movement and breathing into tight areas.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.description: Start on all fours. Slide one arm under the opposite armpit and rotate your torso, allowing your shoulder and head to rest on the floor. Return to center and switch sides. Improves thoracic rotation.

exercises.name: Wall Pec Stretch
exercises.description: Stand next to a wall. Place your forearm flat against it at shoulder height. Gently turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch across your chest and front of your shoulder.

phases.name: Stabilize & Extend
phases.goal: Strengthen postural muscles and build spinal endurance
phases.focus: Scapular Control • Extension Endurance • Postural Stacking

exercises.name: Prone T Raises
exercises.description: Lie face down with arms extended to the sides in a T position. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and raise your arms slightly off the ground. Keep your forehead down and neck relaxed.

exercises.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotations
exercises.description: On hands and knees, place one hand behind your head. Rotate your elbow upward toward the ceiling while keeping your hips still. Slowly return and repeat.

exercises.name: Wall Chin Tucks + Chest Lift
exercises.description: Stand against a wall. Tuck your chin gently and draw your head back. Lift your chest slightly without arching your lower back. Breathe slowly while holding.

exercises.name: Banded Pull-Aparts
exercises.description: Hold a resistance band with your arms straight in front of you. Pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades. Keep shoulders relaxed and arms parallel to the floor.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Rib Expansion Breathing
exercises.description: Lie on one side with your bottom arm extended overhead and knees bent. Place your top hand on your rib cage. Inhale deeply into your side ribs, then exhale slowly. Promotes lateral rib expansion.

phases.name: Integrate & Maintain
phases.goal: Reinforce thoracic freedom and postural strength during dynamic activity
phases.focus: Dynamic Rotation • Postural Resilience • Breath-Backed Movement

exercises.name: Lunge + Overhead Reach
exercises.description: Step into a lunge. Reach the same-side arm overhead, then gently side bend and rotate toward the opposite side. Focus on lengthening through the ribs and upper spine.

exercises.name: Tall Kneeling Band Row + Extension
exercises.description: Kneel upright with a band anchored in front of you. Row the band back while lifting your chest into a subtle thoracic extension. Keep glutes engaged and chin tucked.

exercises.name: Loaded Carry Posture Walk
exercises.description: Hold weights at your sides. Walk slowly while keeping your spine tall, ribs stacked over hips, and shoulders even. Strengthens deep postural stabilizers.

exercises.name: Side Plank with Rotation
exercises.description: Start in a modified side plank on your forearm. Raise your top arm toward the ceiling, then rotate and thread it under your body. Control the movement. Builds oblique and upper spine coordination.

exercises.name: Dynamic Wall Clock Reach
exercises.description: Face a wall. Slowly trace a large arc with one arm in different directions like the numbers of a clock (12, 2, 4, etc.). Maintain shoulder control and steady posture.

lifestyle: Move or perform deep breathing every 30-60 minutes if sitting
Sit on your sit bones (not tailbone) to avoid slouching
Open your chest 3x/day by lifting arms and expanding ribs
Use lumbar and mid-back support when sitting for long periods
plans.maintenance: 2x/week: Mobility drills from Phase 1. 2x/week: Strengthening from Phases 2 & 3. Daily: Breathwork (3-5 minutes).

plans.name: Lumbosacral Disc Recovery Plan
plans.tags: lumbosacral disc recovery L4 L5 S1 herniation bulge sciatica nerve low back
plans.objective: Relieve disc pressure at L4-L5/L5-S1, restore core function, and build long-term spine resilience.

phases.name: Decompress & Calm
phases.goal: Reduce disc pressure, inflammation, and nerve sensitivity
phases.focus: Disc decompression • Nervous system regulation • Gentle mobility

exercises.name: 90-90 Supine Rest Position
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your calves and feet supported on a chair or ottoman so that hips and knees are at 90°. Let your arms relax out to the side, palms up. Breathe deeply through your nose into your belly. Let your low back release into the floor naturally. This calms the nervous system and offloads stress on the lumbar discs.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.description: Remain on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Gently tilt your pelvis back so that your lower back flattens into the floor. Hold for 3 seconds, then release. Restores control and motion in the lumbar segments without compressive force.

exercises.name: Standing Extension Press-Ups
exercises.description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Place both hands on your lower back. Gently press your hips forward and lean backward slightly, looking up with your eyes. Encourages disc material to centralize away from nerve roots. Only move to the edge of comfort.

exercises.name: Seated Sciatic Nerve Glides
exercises.description: Sit at the edge of a firm chair with good posture. Straighten one leg as you pull the toes toward you while simultaneously lifting your head (look up). Slowly return. Mobilizes the sciatic nerve without overstretching it.

exercises.name: Walk & Breathe
exercises.description: Walk at a comfortable pace with arms swinging freely and spine tall. Avoid tensing shoulders or bracing core excessively. Gentle walking promotes disc hydration, joint lubrication, and circulation to healing tissues.

phases.name: Activate & Stabilize
phases.goal: Re-engage deep abdominal and gluteal muscles to stabilize the pelvis and lumbar spine
phases.focus: Core bracing • Glute activation • Postural strength

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees raised to 90° and arms straight toward the ceiling. Brace your core, then slowly lower your right arm and left leg. Keep your back flat on the floor. Return and switch sides. Trains cross-body core coordination and lumbar stability.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.description: Lay on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart. Press through your heels, lifting your hips toward the ceiling while squeezing your glutes. Pause for 3 seconds at the top. Slowly lower back down. Avoid arching through your lower back.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Clamshells
exercises.description: Lie on your side, knees bent and feet stacked. Keeping your feet together, lift your top knee while keeping your hips from rolling backward. May add a light resistance band above the knees. Strengthens glute medius and improves pelvic control.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Begin on all fours. Extend your right arm and left leg at the same time. Keep your hips square and avoid arching or twisting your back. Hold for 5 seconds. Return and switch. Improves core timing and spinal coordination.

exercises.name: Wall Posture Hold
exercises.description: Stand against a wall with your heels, buttocks, upper back, and head touching. Gently tuck your pelvis and lightly brace your core. Hold this stacked alignment while breathing. Strengthens postural muscles and reinforces spinal awareness.

phases.name: Reinforce & Integrate
phases.goal: Reinforce strength and motor control in standing and dynamic movement patterns
phases.focus: Load control • Unilateral stability • Anti-rotation strength

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lie on your back. Extend one leg while keeping the other bent. Drive through the grounded heel to lift your hips evenly. Keep your pelvis level. Hold 2 seconds at the top. Develops unilateral glute and hamstring strength.

exercises.name: Split Stance Pallof Press
exercises.description: Attach a resistance band to your side at chest height. Step into a split stance. Hold the band at your chest, then press it directly forward, resisting rotation. Return slowly. Great for core stability and anti-rotation endurance.

exercises.name: Step-Up + Knee Drive
exercises.description: Use a low box or step. Step up with one foot, driving the opposite knee toward the chest. Pause briefly at the top. Lower slowly. Keeps spine upright while training single-leg strength and dynamic balance.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang naturally. Walk slowly and steadily while keeping your spine vertical. Don't lean or sway. Activates lateral core muscles and strengthens the obliques and QL.

exercises.name: Plank with Shoulder Taps
exercises.description: Start in a high or forearm plank. Tap your opposite shoulder slowly, keeping your hips and shoulders steady. The goal is no twisting. Builds precise control under low back loading.

lifestyle: Switch sitting and standing positions every 30-45 minutes
Use lumbar support if sitting more than 20 minutes
Sleep on your side with a pillow between your knees or on your back with a wedge under knees
Avoid twisting, slouching, or lifting while bent forward
Stay hydrated to nourish discs and tissues
Don't power through pain—movement should reduce discomfort
plans.maintenance: 1x/week: Phase 1 Decompression (great after sitting long or post-travel). 2x/week: Phase 2 Core & Glutes Activation. 1-2x/week: Phase 3 Integration & Strength. Rotate phases based on activity levels or flare-up patterns.

plans.name: Shoulder Stability & Rotator Cuff Rebuild
plans.tags: shoulder stability rotator cuff rebuild impingement frozen shoulder scapular overhead athlete
plans.objective: Restore strength, stability, and control to the shoulder joint targeting rotator cuff and scapular stabilizers.

phases.name: Reset & Mobilize
phases.goal: Calm inflammation, regain safe mobility, reintroduce healthy movement patterns
phases.focus: Pain-free range of motion • Soft tissue hydration • Joint decompression

exercises.name: Pendulum Circles
exercises.description: Lean forward and allow your arm to dangle passively. Use gravity—not muscular force—to gently circle the arm. One of the safest and most effective ways to decompress the joint early in rehab.

exercises.name: Wall Crawls (Flexion & Abduction)
exercises.description: Use your fingers to crawl your hand slowly up a wall, both straight up (flexion) and out to the side (abduction). Focus on control and breathing. Go only as high as is pain-free.

exercises.name: Towel Stretch (Internal Rotation)
exercises.description: Use a towel behind your back like a strap—one hand over the shoulder, the other reaching from below. Gently stretch upward to open the internal rotators. Don't force through sharp pain.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.description: Lying on your side, position the shoulder and elbow at 90°. Use your opposite hand to press the forearm toward the floor. Mobilizes the posterior capsule—a common tight area in injured shoulders.

exercises.name: Scapular Clocks
exercises.description: Visualize a clock over your shoulder blade: 12 (up), 3 (forward), 6 (down), 9 (back). Move your scapula through each position slowly and with control. Improves proprioception and scapular neuromuscular patterning.

phases.name: Activate & Stabilize
phases.goal: Strengthen rotator cuff and teach shoulder blade coordination with arm movement
phases.focus: Scapular stabilization • Cuff recruitment • Postural reeducation

exercises.name: External Rotation with Band
exercises.description: Attach a resistance band to a stable surface. Keep your elbow at your side and rotate outward. Pause at the end range for better control. Directly targets the infraspinatus and teres minor.

exercises.name: Sidelying External Rotation
exercises.description: Lying on your side with a towel between your elbow and ribs, hold a light dumbbell and rotate the forearm toward the ceiling. Slow, deliberate reps are key. Refines rotator cuff coordination.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions
exercises.description: Pinch your shoulder blades together while keeping the rest of your body neutral. Can be done with a resistance band, cable, or lying face down. Trains lower trapezius and rhomboid stability.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: Stand against a wall and slide your arms up into a Y shape, keeping contact with the wall. Trains upward rotation and thoracic extension simultaneously.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raises
exercises.description: Lying face down, lift arms into a Y shape while maintaining a neutral spine. Squeeze shoulder blades down and in. Key drill for rebalancing overhead mechanics and scapular elevation control.

phases.name: Integrate & Reinforce
phases.goal: Transfer strength and control into real-life movement with loaded tasks
phases.focus: Overhead strength • Joint resilience • Integrated stability

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.description: Hold a strong plank. Alternate tapping one shoulder with the opposite hand. Avoid trunk rotation. Engages the entire kinetic chain—core, scapula, and cuff.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.description: Use dumbbells or kettlebells. Keep posture tall and shoulder blades gently retracted. Builds postural awareness, grip endurance, and shoulder stability under load.

exercises.name: Overhead Dumbbell Press (Neutral Grip)
exercises.description: Press dumbbells overhead with palms facing each other. Control the path of the movement. Avoid excessive spinal extension or shrugging. Solidifies end-range shoulder control.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.description: Hold a light resistance band in front of your chest. Pull apart and return slowly. Emphasize the squeeze at the end. Option: diagonal or low-to-high variations.

exercises.name: Partial Turkish Get-Up
exercises.description: Perform the first half of the movement (elbow, hand, bridge). Focus on slow, controlled transitions and shoulder positioning. Excellent for building motor control, proprioception, and long-term durability.

lifestyle: Sleep on your back or unaffected side with a pillow supporting the shoulder and arm
Avoid repeated overhead tasks or heavy loading early in the plan
Alternate arms when carrying grocery bags or backpacks
Perform a posture reset every hour: shoulders back, ribs stacked, neck neutral
Warm up with mobility drills before workouts, especially overhead days
Include thoracic spine mobility (foam rolling, open books) weekly
plans.maintenance: 1x/week: Phase 1 (mobility resets, posterior capsule work). 2x/week: Phase 2 (rotator cuff activation + scapular stability). 1-2x/week: Phase 3 (loaded movement + functional strength). Daily: 1-2 posture resets + 2-3 minutes of scapular engagement.

plans.name: Elbow & Wrist Relief Plan
plans.tags: elbow wrist carpal tunnel tennis golfer epicondylitis ulnar nerve grip forearm
plans.objective: Restore joint balance, reduce pain, and support long-term upper extremity function

phases.name: Unload & Mobilize
phases.goal: Calm inflammation, relieve tight muscles and fascia, and improve joint range of motion without aggravating the area.
phases.focus: Joint decompression • Tendon and nerve mobility • Circulatory improvement

exercises.name: Wrist Circles
exercises.description: Keep the hand relaxed and perform slow, circular wrist movements. Focus on a full, smooth range without clicking or tension. Increases synovial lubrication and resets proprioception.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Extend your arm forward, palm up. Use your opposite hand to gently pull the fingers back toward you. Stretch from the inner forearm to the palm. Breathe and hold tension without bouncing.

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
exercises.description: With the palm down, gently pull the fingers downward and toward your body. Focus on the outer forearm. Great for relieving lateral epicondyle tension.

exercises.name: Fist-to-Finger Extensions
exercises.description: Make a slow, soft fist and open your hand wide, spreading fingers each time. This stimulates blood flow and activates finger extensor and flexor muscles.

exercises.name: Median Nerve Glides
exercises.description: Start with your arm out to the side, palm up. Extend the wrist and fingers, tilt your head to the opposite shoulder, then return. Mobilizes the nerve sheath and reduces neural irritation.

exercises.name: Tendon Gliding Drill
exercises.description: Make a full fist, hook fist, straight fist, and flat fist in sequence. Pause briefly at each stage. Enhances tendon movement through sheaths and improves range.

phases.name: Strengthen & Stabilize
phases.goal: Build strength in the flexors, extensors, and stabilizers of the forearm while improving control through full wrist/elbow range.
phases.focus: Forearm balance • Eccentric control • Functional grip capacity

exercises.name: Wrist Curls (Flexion & Extension)
exercises.description: Support your forearm on a bench or table. Use a light dumbbell to perform controlled wrist curls up and down. Great for both concentric and eccentric muscle strengthening.

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.description: Hold dumbbells with thumbs facing upward. Curl slowly while keeping elbows close to the body. Activates brachioradialis, often overlooked but key to elbow integrity.

exercises.name: Wrist Supination/Pronation with Weight
exercises.description: Hold a hammer or wrench with weight unevenly distributed. Slowly rotate the wrist palm up and down. Strengthens stabilizers that control twist mechanics.

exercises.name: Rubber Band Finger Extensions
exercises.description: Wrap a band around your fingers and open your hand against resistance. Focus on control and pause briefly at full extension.

exercises.name: Grip Squeeze with Soft Ball
exercises.description: Squeeze a therapy ball or grip trainer and hold for 2–3 seconds. Alternate between strong squeezes and pulsing reps for endurance vs. power.

exercises.name: Reverse Tyler Twist (Eccentric Flexor Training)
exercises.description: Use a FlexBar or towel. Load the wrist into flexion and slowly resist as it returns to neutral. Shown to help with medial/lateral epicondylitis.

phases.name: Integrate & Maintain
phases.goal: Reinforce your gains by applying strength and control to real-life motions like lifting, pushing, pulling, and typing.
phases.focus: Endurance • Coordination • Functional movement transfer

exercises.name: Quadruped Wrist Loading
exercises.description: From all fours, gently rock your weight forward and back across your hands. Spread your fingers wide and press evenly through palms. Builds joint tolerance under load.

exercises.name: Neutral Wrist Push-Ups (Elevated or Standard)
exercises.description: Use a neutral fist position or push-up bars to reduce wrist strain. Maintain tight elbows and proper scapular control throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.description: Hold weights and walk upright while bracing your core. Builds grip endurance, coordination, and upper limb alignment through functional load.

exercises.name: Theraband 3D Wrist Training
exercises.description: Anchor a resistance band and move your wrist through all directions: flexion, extension, ulnar deviation, radial deviation, supination, and pronation. Great for sports or active lifestyle demands.

exercises.name: Reaction Toss or Ball Dribble
exercises.description: Dribble a ball in place or bounce it off a wall, alternating hands. Adds speed, accuracy, and upper limb rhythm.

lifestyle: Set up your workstation with ergonomic angles (90° elbow, neutral wrist)
Use gel pads or ergonomic keyboards if typing frequently
Stretch your hands every 30–60 minutes if working at a desk
Don't "push through" early elbow pain—it responds better to frequent, low-impact loading
Alternate carrying bags between hands or use a backpack with even straps
Keep wrists in neutral when lifting weights or using tools
plans.maintenance: 1–2x/week: Phase 1 mobility + neural glide resets. 2x/week: Phase 2 grip and wrist strengthening. 1–2x/week: Phase 3 functional integration and coordination. Daily: 1–2 sets of wrist circles, tendon glides, and nerve flossing.

plans.name: Cervicogenic Headaches / Atlas-Axis Reset (C0–C2)
plans.tags: headache cervicogenic atlas axis C0 C1 C2 upper cervical suboccipital migraine neck
plans.objective: Relieve headache tension, stabilize the upper neck, and reset the brainstem connection

phases.name: Relieve Tension & Realign
phases.goal: Reduce mechanical compression in the upper cervical spine, alleviate suboccipital and fascial tension, and restore normal neural signaling. This phase emphasizes decompression and relaxation.
phases.focus: Suboccipital release • Diaphragmatic regulation • Structural decompression

exercises.name: Suboccipital Release
exercises.description: Lie flat on your back. Place a small massage ball or peanut roller under the base of your skull. Allow the head to settle into the pressure. Slowly rotate your head left and right, stopping on tender spots. Breathe deeply and allow tension to melt. This targets the suboccipital muscles that compress the C0–C2 region and frequently refer pain into the skull and behind the eyes.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.description: Lie flat or sit with one hand on your chest and the other on your belly. Inhale through your nose, expanding the belly first. Exhale slowly through pursed lips. Focus on long, even breaths. Deep breathing resets the vagus nerve, decreases upper trap overactivation, and improves global parasympathetic tone.

exercises.name: Chin Tucks (Supine or Standing)
exercises.description: Gently draw your chin straight back, not down. Imagine sliding your head straight back along the floor or wall. Hold for 3 seconds. Do not allow your head to tilt or rotate. This strengthens deep cervical flexors, realigns the atlas, and minimizes forward head compensation.

exercises.name: Upper Trap & Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.description: Tilt your ear toward your shoulder and gently assist with your opposite hand. Then turn your nose toward your armpit and look down to target the levator. Avoid forcing the stretch. This releases common muscular tension that aggravates C1–C2 misalignment.

exercises.name: Wall Neck Glide Reset
exercises.description: Stand with heels, butt, shoulders, and head against a wall. Glide your head upward as if lifting the crown of your skull toward the ceiling. Avoid chin lift. This promotes axial elongation and upper cervical decompression.

phases.name: Activate & Stabilize
phases.goal: Build deep neck flexor strength, upper cervical control, and shoulder support to maintain proper head posture and reduce dependency on superficial neck muscles.
phases.focus: C0–C2 coordination • Flexor synergy • Postural neuromuscular control

exercises.name: Supine Chin Nod with Resistance
exercises.description: Lie on your back with a soft ball or rolled towel under your head. Nod your chin as if saying "yes," feeling the motion come from just under the skull. Apply gentle resistance with the towel. Focus on control, not force. This isolates longus capitis and longus colli activation—essential for upper cervical stability.

exercises.name: Wall Head Press Isometric
exercises.description: Stand tall with the back of your head touching a wall. Gently press straight back while keeping the chin tucked. Maintain even pressure and natural breathing. Builds static endurance in the postural stabilizers around the occipital ridge.

exercises.name: Neck Rotation Control
exercises.description: While sitting tall or lying down, slowly turn your head left and right through a pain-free range. Keep your motion smooth and avoid snapping or jerking. Focus on tracking the movement with eye alignment and deep stabilizer engagement.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions
exercises.description: Using a resistance band, gently draw the shoulder blades down and together. This resets shoulder alignment and reduces pulling on the cervical spine.

exercises.name: Eye-Head Coordination Drill
exercises.description: Hold your head still and move your eyes in all directions. Then fix your eyes and slowly rotate your head. Improves neurovisual reflexes and re-centers proprioceptive feedback through C1–C2.

phases.name: Integrate & Prevent
phases.goal: Maintain postural alignment and upper cervical stability in daily activities. Strengthen the relationship between neck, spine, visual tracking, and proprioception.
phases.focus: Endurance • Head posture during motion • Brainstem-spine coordination

exercises.name: Wall Walk with Chin Tuck
exercises.description: Stand tall against a wall and slowly raise arms into a Y position. Maintain chin tuck and spinal alignment. Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing deeply. Encourages thoracic extension and deep neck flexor synergy.

exercises.name: Loaded Carry with Postural Awareness
exercises.description: Hold weights in both hands. Walk slowly, focusing on keeping head stacked over shoulders and chin slightly tucked. Maintain a tall spine and light core activation. This functional drill reinforces postural endurance in real-world settings.

exercises.name: Posture Reset + Breath Recalibration
exercises.description: Sit or stand in perfect posture. Take a full inhale through the nose and exhale through the mouth while tucking your chin gently. Repeat while visualizing your spine lengthening and head floating. Recalibrates the nervous system and resets spinal balance.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Cervical Holds
exercises.description: Lie on your side and keep your head aligned with your spine. Lift your head slightly against gravity and hold. Focus on steady breath and gentle engagement. Builds lateral stabilizer strength crucial for rotational control.

exercises.name: Head-Eye Motion Coordination
exercises.description: Use a pen or fingertip at eye level. Fix your eyes and rotate your head side-to-side. Then reverse—hold your head still and track a moving object. Great for athletes, desk workers, or anyone with cervicogenic tension. Rebuilds cervical-visual synchronization and proprioceptive reflexes.

lifestyle: Don't hold your phone between your shoulder and ear—use speaker or headset
Raise your screen to eye level at all workstations (computer, phone, tablet)
Use a contoured pillow that supports your neck's natural curve
Sleep on your side or back; avoid stomach sleeping, which stresses C1–C2
Set hourly posture reminders to check head position
Breathe through your nose to reduce accessory muscle overuse
Avoid sudden or extreme head movements when possible
plans.maintenance: 1–2x/week: Phase 1 decompression and release techniques. 2–3x/week: Phase 2 activation, flexor engagement, and scapular alignment. 1–2x/week: Phase 3 posture, integration, and movement control. Daily: 1–2 posture resets with breathing + chin tucks (1–2 minutes).

plans.name: Tech Neck & Forward Head Posture Recovery Plan
plans.tags: tech neck forward head posture screen slouch kyphosis cervical thoracic desk
plans.objective: Correct alignment, reduce strain, and restore confident posture

phases.name: Unload & Stretch
phases.goal: Decompress the cervical spine, gently stretch chronically overactive muscles, and reduce neural tension. This phase is focused on relief and resetting spinal position without loading.
phases.focus: Muscle release • Cervical unloading • Rib cage and neck mobility

exercises.name: Wall Neck Lengthening
exercises.description: Stand with your back and head flat against a wall. Bring your chin straight back, elongating the back of your neck. You should feel gentle lengthening, not strain. Keep jaw relaxed and breathe slowly. This counters years of forward head posture and reintroduces proper spinal stacking.

exercises.name: Upper Trap Stretch
exercises.description: Sit tall, anchor one hand under your chair, and gently tilt your ear to your opposite shoulder. Use your opposite hand to deepen the stretch slightly. This releases a muscle often overstressed from holding the shoulders up all day.

exercises.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.description: Turn your nose toward your armpit, then gently nod downward. Use your top hand to gently add pressure to the back of your head. Keep your shoulder relaxed. This reduces tightness at the base of the skull where tension headaches often originate.

exercises.name: Thoracic Foam Roller Extensions
exercises.description: Place a foam roller horizontally beneath your upper back. Support your head with your hands, and gently arch back over the roller, breathing into your chest. Move up and down the thoracic spine slowly. Avoid flaring ribs or jamming into discomfort. This restores thoracic extension and prepares your posture for upward realignment.

exercises.name: Chin Tucks (Lying or Standing)
exercises.description: Draw your chin straight back (not down) as if creating a double chin. Hold for 3 seconds. This strengthens the deep neck flexors and resets cervical alignment. Imagine gently sliding your head back along a shelf.

phases.name: Strengthen & Rebalance
phases.goal: Strengthen the neglected stabilizers of the neck, upper back, and shoulders. These postural muscles help hold your head in proper alignment, allowing your body to maintain posture effortlessly throughout the day.
phases.focus: Deep neck flexors • Mid-trap and rhomboid engagement • Scapular stabilization

exercises.name: Prone Y Raises
exercises.description: Lie face down with arms overhead in a "Y" shape. Gently lift arms while squeezing your shoulder blades downward. Keep forehead on the mat. Avoid shrugging shoulders. This improves the mid and lower traps that counteract hunching.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.description: Stand with your heels, butt, shoulders, and head against a wall. Begin with elbows at 90° (goal post position) and slowly raise your arms overhead, maintaining wall contact. Don't let your lower back arch. This retrains the scapular rhythm and strengthens postural reflexes.

exercises.name: Banded Chin Tuck Press
exercises.description: Place a light resistance band around the back of your head, holding both ends forward. Tuck your chin straight back and press gently into the resistance. Hold briefly, then release. This directly strengthens the deep neck flexors needed for upright posture.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions
exercises.description: Using a band or light cable, pull your elbows back while squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your neck long and chest lifted. Avoid shrugging. This balances anterior and posterior shoulder control.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Head Holds
exercises.description: Stand with your head against the wall and perform a light chin tuck. Press your head into the wall while maintaining a tall spine. Breathe naturally. This isometric drill teaches endurance in the deep stabilizers of the neck and upper back.

phases.name: Integrate & Maintain
phases.goal: Translate better posture into your day-to-day life and build lasting posture endurance. This phase strengthens your ability to hold good alignment while moving, sitting, working, or walking.
phases.focus: Posture integration • Gait and carry mechanics • Habitual stacking of the spine

exercises.name: Loaded Carry with Chin Tuck
exercises.description: Hold dumbbells or bags by your sides. Stand tall, gently tuck your chin, and walk slowly. Keep your shoulders level and avoid arching your low back. This trains your spine to hold a stacked position under real-world stress.

exercises.name: Seated Posture Holds
exercises.description: Sit tall in a chair without back support. Stack your ears over shoulders, ribs over hips. Slightly brace your core. Breathe deeply and hold. This builds postural stamina for desk work and daily tasks.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Neck Isometric Holds
exercises.description: Lie on your side with head in neutral. Gently press your head into the air (against gravity) as if resisting a downward force. Avoid tilting or sagging. Improves lateral neck control.

exercises.name: Thoracic Band Rows
exercises.description: Attach a resistance band to shoulder height. Row back by pulling your elbows toward your ribs, squeezing shoulder blades. Maintain a long neck and neutral spine. This strengthens thoracic extensors to keep your upper back upright.

exercises.name: Chin Tuck + Overhead Reach
exercises.description: Tuck your chin and raise both arms overhead slowly. Maintain posture throughout the reach. This reinforces cervical alignment while activating the shoulder complex in upward motion.

lifestyle: Position screens at eye level; avoid looking down for extended periods
Use standing desks or alternate between seated and standing positions
Sit on the edge of your chair with your feet flat and chest lifted
Take micro breaks every 30 minutes to reset posture and stretch
Perform 5–10 chin tucks throughout the day when using devices
Stretch your pecs regularly to counteract forward pull
Sleep on your back with a supportive pillow or on your side with neck aligned
Avoid stomach sleeping or thick pillows that push the head forward
plans.maintenance: 2x/week: Phase 1 (decompression and release). 2–3x/week: Phase 2 (strength and alignment). 1–2x/week: Phase 3 (integration and endurance). Daily: 1–2 posture checks with chin tucks, especially during screen time.

plans.name: Lumbar Facet Syndrome / Extension Intolerance Recovery Plan
plans.tags: lumbar facet low back extension standing pain spine stiffness morning
plans.objective: For sharp low back pain, standing discomfort, and postural correction

phases.name: Relieve & Decompress
phases.goal: Reduce compression in the facet joints, release tight musculature, and restore movement through supported flexion patterns.
phases.focus: Flexion-based relief • Posterior chain lengthening • Nervous system calm

exercises.name: Child's Pose Stretch
exercises.description: Begin in a kneeling position. Sit your hips back onto your heels, bring your knees wide, and extend your arms forward. Rest your forehead on the floor. Breathe into your back and feel your ribs expand. This resets lumbar tension and is one of the safest and most effective ways to decompress the posterior chain.

exercises.name: Supine Knees-to-Chest
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your knees bent. Pull both knees gently toward your chest using your hands. Hold, breathe deeply, and allow your spine to round naturally. This stretches the erector spinae and provides near-instant relief from extension-based compression.

exercises.name: Posterior Pelvic Tilts
exercises.description: Remain on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Flatten your lower back into the floor by gently tucking your pelvis. Engage your lower abdominals. This movement retrains the body to find pelvic neutrality.

exercises.name: Hamstring Wall Stretch
exercises.description: Lie on your back near a doorway or wall corner. Extend one leg up the wall, maintaining a slight bend in the knee. The opposite leg stays flat. Flex your foot back toward your face. This reduces tightness in the hamstrings that can tug on the pelvis and aggravate facet joint pain.

exercises.name: Seated Cat-Cow
exercises.description: Sit upright in a sturdy chair. Inhale and gently arch your spine, pulling your chest forward. Exhale and round your spine, tucking your chin and pelvis under. Move slowly and with control. This variation provides a safe way to move the spine without strain.

phases.name: Activate & Align
phases.goal: Rebuild stability in the core and glutes while restoring balance to the lumbar-pelvic region. This helps reduce lumbar joint stress and guards against hyperextension patterns.
phases.focus: Core engagement • Posterior chain activation • Anti-extension patterning

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your arms straight up and knees bent at 90°. Brace your core, flatten your back into the floor, and slowly extend one leg and the opposite arm. Keep movements slow and steady. Do not let your back arch. Switch sides. This reinforces deep core control.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges (Tucked Pelvis)
exercises.description: Lay on your back, knees bent. Before lifting, gently tuck your pelvis to prevent your lower back from arching. Drive through your heels and lift your hips, focusing on squeezing the glutes. Slowly lower with control. This encourages proper glute dominance over low back compensation.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Clamshells
exercises.description: Lie on your side with hips stacked, knees bent. Keep your feet together and lift your top knee. Do not let your hips rotate back. Use a resistance band above your knees for increased challenge. Strengthens glute medius to improve pelvic alignment.

exercises.name: Modified Curl-Ups
exercises.description: Lie flat on your back with one leg bent and the other straight. Place hands under the lumbar curve. Exhale and lift your head and upper shoulders, engaging your upper abdominals. Keep the movement small and controlled. Do not pull on your neck.

exercises.name: All-Fours Rock Back
exercises.description: Begin on hands and knees. Maintain a neutral spine as you slowly shift your hips back toward your heels. Do not round the spine excessively. Breathe in as you return forward. This teaches pelvic control in a non-threatening position.

phases.name: Reinforce & Functionalize
phases.goal: Integrate spinal stabilization into daily function. Build long-term control and resilience through posture, strength, and anti-extension control.
phases.focus: Posture endurance • Core-braced motion • Glute-driven strength

exercises.name: Tall Kneeling Band Press
exercises.description: In a tall kneeling position (knees on the ground, hips forward), hold a resistance band at chest height. Press forward slowly, keeping your ribs stacked over your pelvis. Brace your core. Do not allow your spine to arch as the band adds resistance.

exercises.name: Wall Sit with Core Bracing
exercises.description: Stand against a wall and slide down until thighs are parallel to the floor. Press your lower back gently into the wall. Brace your abs and breathe. This builds lower-body endurance while training spinal stability in a compressed position.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Return to hands and knees. Extend one arm and opposite leg. Hold for 5 seconds, ensuring hips remain level. Avoid swaying or arching the lower back. Improves core integrity under cross-body movement.

exercises.name: Step-Downs
exercises.description: Stand on a low step. Slowly lower your opposite foot to the floor while keeping your hips level. Avoid rotating your torso or arching your back. Strengthens quads, glutes, and spinal alignment during descent.

exercises.name: Loaded Marches
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Stand tall and slowly lift one knee up, then alternate. Do not lean back. Focus on keeping your ribcage down and pelvis neutral. Great for reinforcing core-braced gait mechanics.

lifestyle: Use a footrest or staggered stance if standing for long periods
Avoid overreaching overhead or hyperextending your spine
Sit with lumbar support and feet flat
Take microbreaks every 30–45 minutes if sedentary
Stretch your hips and hamstrings regularly
Sleep on your side with a pillow between your knees or on your back with a pillow under your knees
plans.maintenance: 2x/week: Phase 1 decompression and flexibility recovery. 2x/week: Phase 2 core and glute activation. 1x/week: Phase 3 functional strength and posture drills. Track pain triggers, postural habits, and progress weekly.

plans.name: Knee Rebuild Plan (Tracking / Tendon / Arthritis)
plans.tags: knee patellar tracking tendon arthritis quad patella tendonitis osteoarthritis
plans.objective: Stabilize the knee, reduce pain, and rebuild lifelong function

phases.name: Reset & Activate
phases.goal: Calm irritation, reduce inflammation, and reintroduce gentle movement and quad activation. This phase establishes the foundation of neuromuscular control.
phases.focus: Quad isometrics • Joint decompression • Pain-free motion retraining

exercises.name: Quad Set (Isometric)
exercises.description: Sit on the floor or a bed with your leg extended. Contract your quad muscle to press your knee firmly into the floor. Hold for 5–7 seconds. Helps wake up the quadriceps without bending the joint.

exercises.name: Heel Slides
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees extended. Slowly slide your heel toward your buttock, flexing the knee, then return to the start. A safe way to restore range of motion early on.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.description: With one knee bent and the other extended, lift the straight leg 45°, hold for 3 seconds, then lower. Promotes quad strength while protecting sensitive tissue.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch
exercises.description: Place hands on a wall, step one foot back, and stretch the calf with both a straight and bent back knee. Loosens tight posterior chain muscles affecting knee tracking.

exercises.name: Seated Patellar Glides
exercises.description: Sit with your leg outstretched and relaxed. Using your fingers, gently glide the kneecap up, down, left, and right. Maintains mobility of the patella and prevents early stiffness.

exercises.name: Foam Roll Quads + IT Band
exercises.description: Use a foam roller to release tension in the quadriceps and iliotibial band. Avoid directly rolling over the knee cap. Helps reduce fascial restriction.

phases.name: Strengthen & Stabilize
phases.goal: Rebuild the muscular support system around the knee while correcting movement patterns and tracking errors. Introduce light resistance and focus on control.
phases.focus: Eccentric quad strength • Hip/knee alignment • Multi-muscle coordination

exercises.name: Terminal Knee Extension (TKE)
exercises.description: Secure a resistance band behind the knee. Slowly extend the knee while squeezing the quad. Control the return. Essential for full extension and patellar positioning.

exercises.name: Step-Ups (Low Box)
exercises.description: Use a 6–12" box. Step up with one leg while focusing on keeping the knee over the ankle. Avoid leaning or collapsing inward.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with Band
exercises.description: Lie on your back with band above your knees. Press knees outward and lift hips off the floor, squeezing the glutes. Builds posterior chain strength to stabilize the pelvis and knee.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.description: Slide down a wall until knees are bent at 90°, weight in heels. Engage quads, glutes, and core. Increase time as tolerated.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.description: Slowly rise onto your toes, then lower under control. Improves ankle-knee synchronization and supports push-off strength.

exercises.name: Clamshells with Band
exercises.description: Lie on your side with band above the knees. Keep feet together and lift the top knee. Strengthens glute medius to correct knee valgus.

phases.name: Functional Reinforcement
phases.goal: Translate strength into everyday movement, enhance joint integrity, and prevent flare-ups through control under load.
phases.focus: Dynamic knee loading • Single-leg control • Tendon reconditioning

exercises.name: Reverse Lunges
exercises.description: Step back into a lunge, keeping the front knee stacked over the ankle. Push through the front heel to return. Reduces anterior knee load compared to forward lunges.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance + Reach
exercises.description: Stand on one leg and reach the opposite hand forward and down, maintaining alignment and control. Excellent for knee proprioception and glute engagement.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.description: Place a band above the knees. Step side to side in a semi-squat. Maintains hip-knee alignment and improves lateral stability.

exercises.name: Wall Ball Squats
exercises.description: Use a stability ball between your back and the wall. Squat down to 90°, keeping knees in line with feet. Encourages safe loading through full range.

exercises.name: Jump Rope or Hop Matrix
exercises.description: If pain-free, use light jump rope or forward/lateral hops to condition the tendons and prepare for impact activity.

lifestyle: Sit with feet flat and avoid crossing legs for long periods
Use ice or compression wraps if swelling persists post-activity
Avoid deep squats with poor control or knee pain
Strengthen hips and ankles to support the knee's mechanical chain
Use knee sleeves or braces only when needed for heavy loading—not as a crutch
plans.maintenance: 1–2x/week: Phase 1 mobility resets and quad activation. 2x/week: Phase 2 strength-focused sessions. 1–2x/week: Functional movement and Phase 3 exercises. Daily: 5-minute alignment check and 2 mobility drills (ex. calf stretch + TKE).

plans.name: Ankle & Foot Realignment Plan
plans.tags: ankle foot arch flat feet plantar fasciitis achilles pronation supination balance gait
plans.objective: Restore your foundation, stabilize your stride, and reduce long-term strain

phases.name: Mobilize & Activate
phases.goal: Improve mobility, reawaken sensory input, and rebuild neuromuscular awareness in the foot and ankle.
phases.focus: Fascial release • Intrinsic muscle activation • Basic joint mobility

exercises.name: Foot Rolling (Lacrosse Ball or Roller)
exercises.description: Stand or sit and roll the plantar surface of the foot on a firm ball. Move from the heel to the ball of the foot, pausing on tight or tender areas. This helps improve circulation, fascial mobility, and nerve input.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.description: Either seated or lying down, perform large, slow, deliberate circles at the ankle. Move through full dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion, and eversion. Don't rush. This helps to decompress stiff joints and improve multi-planar mobility.

exercises.name: Toe Yoga
exercises.description: Lift the big toe while pressing the other toes down, then reverse. Do this slowly and with intention. It targets the intrinsic foot muscles and helps restore arch activation and toe independence.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch (Knee Straight & Bent)
exercises.description: Stand facing a wall. Stretch the gastrocnemius with a straight back leg, then bend the knee slightly to stretch the soleus. Ankle dorsiflexion is critical to functional gait and squat patterns.
